Video review

Their open-ear design, stable Bluetooth connection, SpeedNova low-latency technology, and surprisingly clean, wide sound have completely changed my mind about wireless headphones.

Open-Ear Gaming Earbuds? Meet the ROG Cetra Open Wireless

It's a great format for sports, and it's very comfortable for gaming sessions. For a streamer who sits for five, six, or more hours and doesn't want anything pressing on their head.

This device is for active gamers who are a little older—people who need to work, work out, just listen to music, have a drink, and play games—all with a single device.

These are probably the best headphones of this form factor that I've ever tested.

Media review

IGN

Asus is basically creating a new niche here and one that I have personally been waiting for. I play games most days for work but I need to be able to hear what's going on around me, whether that's my wife talking, a delivery at the front door, or a crying baby. I find earbuds more comfortable than headsets but "transparency modes" on existing gaming earbuds are universally terrible. Open earbuds – so-named because they sit outside your ear canal – are far better for hearing what's happening.
